featured_article.title: How lift is generated: Bernoulli vs Newton explanations
featured_article.excerpt: While many students learn that airplane wings generate lift solely through Bernoulli's principle (faster airflow over the curved top creates lower pressure), the complete picture is far more fascinating: **Newton's third law plays the equally crucial role** as wings deflect massive amounts of air downward, creating an equal and opposite upward force. Think of it this way—a wing doesn't just "surf" on pressure differences, it actively **punches down tons of air every second**, and that air punches back with enough force to lift a 500-ton jumbo jet into the sky! Both explanations work together in nature, showing how the same physical phenomenon can be understood through multiple complementary principles of physics.

topic_highlights.title: International Space Station science experiments
topic_highlights.blurb: The International Space Station serves as a unique laboratory where scientists conduct experiments in microgravity, studying everything from protein crystal growth to combustion flames that burn in perfect spheres impossible to create on Earth. These weightless conditions reveal fundamental physics principles and help develop technologies essential for long-duration space missions to Mars and beyond, while also advancing medical treatments and materials science here on Earth.

topic_highlights.title: Gravitational waves and what they tell us about...
topic_highlights.blurb: Gravitational waves are ripples in the fabric of spacetime itself, created when massive objects like black holes collide and literally stretch and compress the universe around us. These cosmic messengers allow us to "hear" the universe in an entirely new way, revealing hidden black hole mergers, neutron star crashes, and potentially even echoes from the Big Bang that could revolutionize our understanding of physics and guide future space exploration.

topic_highlights.title: Mars Perseverance rover sample collection updates
topic_highlights.blurb: NASA's Perseverance rover has successfully collected over 20 rock and soil samples from Mars' Jezero Crater, preserving potential evidence of ancient microbial life in sealed tubes for future retrieval. This groundbreaking sample caching mission represents humanity's first step toward confirming extraterrestrial life and will revolutionize our understanding of planetary evolution when the samples return to Earth in the 2030s.
